desc:
Each interval [start, end] is closed: it contains every integer day from start to end inclusive. Two intervals that share even one day overlap, so [1, 3] and [3, 5] overlap.

Split the intervals into groups so that no two intervals in the same group overlap, using as few groups as possible. To make the answer unique, build the groups with this rule: handle the intervals in order of increasing start (ties broken by smaller input index), and put each interval into the lowest-numbered existing group whose latest interval ended before this interval starts; if no such group exists, open a new group with the next number. Groups are numbered 1, 2, 3, ... in the order they are opened.

Return an array whose i-th element is the group number of intervals[i].

intervals = [[1, 3], [2, 5], [4, 6], [3, 8]]
result = [1, 2, 1, 3]

The largest label in the result is the minimum number of groups.
hints: Process the intervals from left to right by start time. For the current interval, which groups could it join?
A group is available when the end of its last interval is strictly smaller than the current start. You need the lowest-numbered available group quickly.

Keep a min-heap of busy groups keyed by their last end and a min-heap of free group numbers. Before placing an interval, move every busy group whose end is smaller than the start to the free heap; then take the smallest free number or open a new group.
editorial: This is interval partitioning (colouring an interval graph). Sort indices by (start, index). Maintain two heaps: busy holds pairs (end, group) for groups whose last interval is still running, free holds numbers of groups that can take a new interval. For the current interval, pop from busy while end < start and push those group numbers to free. Since starts never decrease, a group that became free stays free for all later intervals. Then take heappop(free) if there is one, else open group count + 1; push (end, group) to busy.

The number of groups opened equals the largest number of intervals that cover a common day, which is also a lower bound, so the partition is optimal. Each interval is pushed and popped a constant number of times: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
solution:
import heapq


def assignGroups(intervals):
    n = len(intervals)
    order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: (intervals[i][0], i))
    busy = []
    free = []
    groups = 0
    labels = [0] * n
    for i in order:
        s, e = intervals[i]
        while busy and busy[0][0] < s:
            heapq.heappush(free, heapq.heappop(busy)[1])
        if free:
            g = heapq.heappop(free)
        else:
            groups += 1
            g = groups
        labels[i] = g
        heapq.heappush(busy, (e, g))
    return labels
